catalogue_title: Mass increase and acyclic cancellation for phase flows on quiver complexes
title: Mass increase and acyclic cancellation for phase flows on quiver complexes
label: Stability and Geometric Degeneration · Paper 11

abstract_html: For two-term complexes over a two-vertex parallel-arrow quiver, with degree-one term supported at the source, trace-norm mass can increase along the Haiden–Katzarkov–Kontsevich–Pandit phase flow defined by positivity. We give an explicit noncommuting example. Nevertheless, for invertible source differential and vertex charges in the strict upper half-plane, every positive initial metric yields exponential decay of the acyclic coefficients and convergence of the normalized cohomology metric. For charges −1+i and 1+i and initially balanced cohomology, a sufficiently large least acyclic singular value gives quantitative cancellation for arbitrary surviving dimension, acyclic rank and bounded mixing. The estimates are independent of the number of arrows, the surviving stabilizer and the acyclic condition number. The evolving coefficient approaches its instantaneous cohomology coefficient, and the surviving moment-map defects tend to zero. The proof controls the polar phase using only the nonsingular cohomology block. As a scalar differential scale tends to infinity, the static mass and its first derivatives in bounded arrow coordinates converge uniformly. A rescaled profile forces third derivatives to diverge. The real phase combination of an explicit metric primitive has a negative Levi direction on a complex gauge orbit and identifies the positive limiting cohomology potential.
